purpose: Independent practice of B1.3 — comparing two-digit numbers up to 50 and ordering small sets.
student_learning_goal: I can compare two numbers up to 50 and order a small set from smallest to biggest.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can compare two numbers up to 50 and order a small set from smallest to biggest.
header.character_watermark: Lila in the top-right corner, holding a jar of buttons. Small (~1.5in tall).

parts.student_instructions: Compare each pair. Write > for greater than, < for less than, or = if equal.
parts.visual_layout: Top third of the page. Six comparison rows. Each row shows two numbers with a blank in the middle for the symbol. Pairs: 12 vs 21, 35 vs 38, 47 vs 23, 30 vs 30, 41 vs 38, 25 vs 50.

image_placeholders.description: Six comparison rows in B&W line-art, stacked vertically. Each row: number on left in a box, blank circle in middle for the symbol, number on right in a box. Pairs: 12 vs 21, 35 vs 38, 47 vs 23, 30 vs 30, 41 vs 38, 25 vs 50.
image_placeholders.placement: Top third of the page; full-width.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P1_SIX_COMPARES: keywords (compare, greater, less) name what the symbols indicate.

parts.student_instructions: Two ordering tasks. Task A: order from SMALLEST to BIGGEST. Task B: order from BIGGEST to SMALLEST.
parts.visual_layout: Middle of the page. Two ordering tasks. Task A: 4 number cards (15, 32, 8, 25) at top with blank arrows pointing right; child writes the order. Task B: 5 number cards (47, 30, 41, 35, 50) at top with blank arrows pointing right; child writes the order.

image_placeholders.description: Two ordering tasks in B&W line-art, stacked vertically. Task A header: 'Smallest to Biggest'. Below the header, 4 number cards (15, 32, 8, 25) in a row. Below the cards, 4 ordered blank slots with right-arrows. Task B header: 'Biggest to Smallest'. Below: 5 number cards (47, 30, 41, 35, 50). Below: 5 ordered blank slots.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P2_ORDER_TASKS: keywords (order, smallest, biggest) name what the tasks ask for.

parts.student_instructions: Pick THREE numbers between 20 and 50. Order them. Write a sentence explaining HOW you decided which was biggest.
parts.visual_layout: Bottom of the page. Three blank number-boxes at the top. Below: a 'smallest to biggest' line with three blank slots. Below that: a sentence-starter line: 'I knew ___ was biggest because ___.'

image_placeholders.description: An open three-number ordering area in B&W line-art. Top: three blank number boxes (each ~1.5in × 1.5in). Middle: a horizontal line with three blank slots and right-arrows. Bottom: a sentence-starter line.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P3_MY_NUMBERS: keywords (numbers, biggest, order) name what the area asks for.

parts.answer_key: Open. Accept any 3 numbers 20-50 ordered correctly. Look for the explanation: ideal answer cites 'tens-first reasoning' (e.g. 'I knew 47 was biggest because it had 4 tens and the others had 3').'

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, pick FIVE numbers between 30 and 50. Order them from biggest to smallest!
teacher_notes: Lesson 4 consolidation. Hand out at the end of partner stations. Watch for: (a) Part 1 children who flip > and < — they may know the relationship but not the symbols; (b) Part 3 children who explain by saying 'it just looks bigger' rather than citing tens — flag for re-loop on tens-first reasoning. Use Part 3 as evidence for the formative tracker column 'uses tens-first reasoning'.
